clue.text: City's second to embargo cheese sandwiches

indicators.note: the cheese is the bread around a filling, so it encloses the other pieces

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
to embargo something is to ban it

explanation.surface: A city's second-in-command bans the import of cheese sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' looks like a rank in the city's hierarchy, but it is only an abbreviation; 'sandwiches' makes the cheese the bread around the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Brisbane is the capital city of Queensland, Australia.

clue.text: Flatter live comedian (but only his first half)

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist

indicators.note: only the front half of the word comedian is kept, its first four letters

explanation.surface: A live comedian is flattered, though only half his act lands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flatter' is the verb meaning to suit someone, as a dress flatters its wearer; the parenthesis keeps COME from COMEDIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes that suit or show someone off to advantage are said to flatter them; same sense of a verb.

clue.text: Angry cult exposed independent umpire first

indicators.note: first says the independent umpire pieces come before the cult remnant

parts.note: a referee, or ref, does the umpire's job

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of its outer covering, so the word cult loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An independent umpire, angered, exposes a cult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' moves I and REF ahead of UL, the exposed core of 'cult'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireful is a literary adjective meaning full of ire, i.e. wrathful or furious.

clue.text: Harrass first to take Ecstasy

indicators.note: to take means to swallow, so the first word holds the drug inside it

parts.note: to come first is to be best
E is the street abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A warning about being pestered into trying ecstasy for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harrass' is the clue's own misspelling of harass.
explanation.definitionFit: To be beset is to be troubled or hounded persistently, a synonym for being harassed.

clue.text: Greek character performing dance that's slightly different

parts.note: nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters of the word dance are put through their paces into a new order

explanation.surface: A Greek actor performs a dance with a subtle twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nuanced has fine shades of distinction, so it is only subtly different.

clue.text: Like bottom to be pert?

definitions.meaning: a cheek is one buttock, so a bottom is made of them

explanation.surface: Wondering whether having a bottom makes one saucy.
explanation.definitionFit: Impudent, saucy behaviour is called cheeky; the playful first reading uses cheek as buttock.

clue.text: Avengers actress has condition in contract initially granting respect

parts.note: Honor Blackman played Cathy Gale in the 1960s British TV series The Avengers
if introduces a condition

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letters of the words in and contract

explanation.surface: A star of The Avengers has a respectful clause written into her contract.
explanation.walkthrough: The Avengers here is the 1960s British spy series, not the Marvel films.
explanation.definitionFit: An honorific is a title or form of address that conveys esteem, as in Sir or Dame.

clue.text: Nurse holding most of film with church's testimony

indicators.note: holding means the nurse encloses the shortened film

parts.note: EN is an enrolled nurse

indicators.note: most of means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a video is a recorded film
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A nurse with a church film gives her testimony.
explanation.definitionFit: Testimony given in court is evidence, the material offered as proof.

clue.text: Tyrol trek regularly includes house in National Park

indicators.note: includes means the selected letters wrap around the house
regularly takes every other letter of Tyrol trek, starting from the second

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house

explanation.surface: A walking trip in the Tyrol takes in a house in a National Park.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tyrol is Alpine, but the park is in California; SEMI is a British semi-detached house, one of a pair sharing a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Yosemite is a famous national park in California's Sierra Nevada.

clue.text: King, perhaps, shames lunatic wearing hollow crown

indicators.note: wearing means the outer letters sit on the scrambled ones like a hat
hollow means the middle of the word crown is emptied, leaving its ends
lunatic means the letters of shames are crazily mixed

explanation.surface: A king shamed by a lunatic who wears an empty crown.
explanation.definitionFit: The king is one of the pieces in chess, an example of the category.

clue.text: In the end, Ramone sings punk rock

indicators.note: punk suggests the letters are thrown about rebelliously
in the end takes the last letter of the name Ramone

explanation.surface: Punk rocker Joey Ramone sings punk rock to the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punk rock' looks like a genre, but 'punk' is the anagram signal and 'rock' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Gneiss is a banded metamorphic rock, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Journalist sent north and south for legal document

indicators.note: and south means the same journalist is then written downwards as normal
sent north in a down clue means the journalist reads upwards

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A journalist is despatched north and south to fetch a legal paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed is a signed legal instrument, such as one conveying property.

clue.text: Chat about being hugged by timid person — it could be ticklish close up

definitions.text: it could be ticklish close up

indicators.note: being hugged by means the rearranged letters sit inside the timid person

parts.note: a mouse is a shy, timid person

indicators.note: about signals the letters of chat moved around

explanation.surface: Chatting while being hugged by a shy person, whose upper lip tickles at close quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Facial hair on the upper lip would tickle someone kissed or hugged at close range.

clue.text: Discharge that man overcome by drink

indicators.note: overcome by means the man is surrounded by the drink

parts.note: rum is a spirit
he is that man

explanation.surface: A man overcome by drink leaves a discharge.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is a watery mucus discharge from the eyes or nose.

clue.text: Took drugs? Took drugs without sailor

indicators.note: without means lacking the sailor

parts.note: to have abused substances is to have taken drugs
AB is an able seaman

explanation.surface: A question and a statement about drug-taking, minus a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter repeats the phrase on purpose: the first time it defines, the second time it is a longer synonym that loses an able seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Drug users are said to use, so someone who used took drugs.

clue.text: Colt's offspring? No way!

definitions.meaning: a Colt is a revolver, so its child is the child of a firearm
an exclamation of surprise or disbelief

explanation.surface: A young horse's foal, or an exclamation of disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: Colt suggests a young horse; here it is the Colt revolver.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a mild American exclamation of surprise; literally the child of a firearm.

clue.text: Sure to take over old company making a loss

indicators.note: to take over means to swallow up the company inside

parts.note: deft means sure-handed, skilful
ICI was Imperial Chemical Industries, a former British company

explanation.surface: A confident takeover of an old firm ends in loss.
explanation.definitionFit: A deficit is a shortfall, the amount by which spending exceeds income.

clue.text: Armstrong, perhaps, finally faces Anderson or Broad?

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of faces

parts.note: James Anderson and Stuart Broad were England's leading fast bowlers in cricket

explanation.surface: Neil Armstrong finally faces England's bowlers.
explanation.walkthrough: PACEMAN is a cricket term for a fast bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: Neil Armstrong, the first moonwalker, is an example of an astronaut.

clue.text: Unnatural air formed in rising depressions

indicators.note: in places the shaped letters inside the reversed depressions
rising in a down clue means the word reads upwards

parts.note: dents are small depressions

indicators.note: formed means the letters of air are shaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Air formed into rising hollows looks unnatural.
explanation.definitionFit: A strained manner is forced and lacks ease, so it seems artificial.

clue.text: Heartless tyke's invested in tripe copyrights

indicators.note: invested in means put inside

parts.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, nonsense

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle of the word tyke, keeping its ends

explanation.surface: A heartless rascal's money is tied up in tripe.
explanation.walkthrough: TYKE is a mischievous child; PANTS is British slang for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Patents and copyrights are both forms of intellectual-property protection, one used loosely for the other.

clue.text: Fall off shack

definitions.meaning: to cast or let drop, as a tree drops leaves

explanation.definitionFit: A tree sheds leaves when they drop away; a garden hut is the noun sense.

clue.text: Clothing that's a hit

definitions.meaning: an item worn on the foot

explanation.surface: An outfit that is a smash success.
explanation.definitionFit: Footwear knitted to cover the foot, and slang for a hard punch.

clue.text: Cult leader leaves animal part

parts.note: a sect is a religious group or cult

indicators.note: leader leaves means the animal's first letter goes

parts.note: a lion is a big cat

explanation.surface: A cult's leader quits and an animal stays behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A section is a portion or division of something, one part of the whole.

clue.text: BBC One release

parts.note: a means one
to untie is to set free

explanation.surface: An announcement of a new release on BBC One.
explanation.walkthrough: 'BBC One' reads as the channel, but splits: the BBC is the definition and One gives A.
explanation.definitionFit: Auntie, or Auntie Beeb, is a long-standing British nickname for the BBC.

clue.text: Run to be embraced by padre, out-of-uniform man of the cloth

indicators.note: to be embraced by means the run sits inside the reworked padre
out of uniform means the letters of padre are no longer in order

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A padre out of uniform is caught running, a priest in mufti.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man of the cloth' usually means a priest; here it is a cloth merchant.
explanation.definitionFit: A draper sells fabric, so is literally a man dealing in cloth.

clue.text: Rubbish place to eat in hospital? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: in seems to put the café inside the hospital
quite the opposite reverses the containment, so the hospital goes inside

parts.note: a caff is British slang for a cheap café

explanation.surface: A rubbish eatery in a hospital, or is it the other way round?
explanation.walkthrough: CAFF is British slang for a cheap café.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaff is husks separated from grain, hence worthless stuff or rubbish.

clue.text: Man at No.11 leads this game, cut short by former partner

indicators.note: by means next to, the ex standing beside the game

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: Chequers is the British name for the board game draughts

explanation.surface: The Chancellor's game is ended early by an ex.
explanation.walkthrough: No.11 Downing Street is the home of the British Chancellor of the Exchequer; Chequers is also the PM's country house.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chancellor at No. 11 Downing Street heads the Treasury department named in this office.

clue.text: Episode five bores mixed-up teen

indicators.note: bores means drills into, so five goes inside
mixed-up means the letters of teen are scrambled

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: An episode where five things bore a confused teenager.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is an incident or happening, much like an episode.

clue.text: Household servants get older

parts.note: men is an old word for male servants
to age is to grow older

explanation.surface: The household servants are getting on.
explanation.definitionFit: A ménage is a domestic establishment, the members of a home.

clue.text: Avoid drink when harnessing unruly steed

indicators.note: harnessing means the drink straps itself around the horse letters

parts.note: a sip is a small drink

indicators.note: unruly means the letters of steed run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Avoid having a drink while tacking up a wild horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidestep a question or a blow is to dodge it, a synonym of evade.

clue.text: Dancing with this girl, Tom could get nominated

indicators.note: dancing means the letters of the girl's name and Tom move together into a new order

explanation.surface: Tom gets a nomination for dancing with a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: The girl's name and TOM together rearrange into NOMINATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Nadine is a female given name, so is a girl in crossword terms.

clue.text: Woolly winter tops to keep active?

definitions.text: Woolly winter tops to keep active?

indicators.note: woolly means fuzzy and confused, so these letters are muddled
tops picks the first letters of keep and active

explanation.surface: Woolly winter jumpers to keep one going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tops' means both the clothes and the first letters K and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Knitted jumpers and cardigans are warm wool garments worn in winter.
